independent_review.additional_reading: The registered 10.2.1.3 catalogue (doc/catalogues/assignment.json) and its rendered view were read in full, because the ownership boundary was the central question.
independent_review.why_this_scope_is_high_risk: Assignment is one of the richest areas in the standard for runtime-observable effects, and the already-registered 10.2.1.3 sits in the middle of this packet's scope. The failure modes are symmetric: claiming an effect 10.2.1.3 already owns, or punting a rule that these sections genuinely own.

zero_permissions_adjudication.claim: no normative unit in scope grants processor latitude
zero_permissions_adjudication.detail: No normative unit in 10.2.1.1, 10.2.1.2, 10.2.1.4 or 10.2.1.5 grants the processor latitude. The conditional admissions in 10.2.1.2 - the 'unless' and 'otherwise' clauses - are program eligibility restrictions, not processor permissions.
zero_permissions_adjudication.the_note: The sentence permitting pure elemental subroutine assignments to be performed simultaneously or in any order occurs ONLY in the unnumbered NOTE in 10.2.1.5. Dispositioning the note and all its fine units as informative is correct, and the plans appropriately forbid order, simultaneity, temporary, side-effect and call-count oracles.
zero_permissions_adjudication.contrast: 10.2.1.3, which is out of scope here, does contain normative processor latitude at p4, p7 and p16, already recorded as permissions in its own catalogue. The contrast confirms the distinction was drawn deliberately rather than missed.

table_10_8_review.note: Conversion is left to 10.2.1.3 p13; this scope owns only Table 10.8 eligibility.

character_length_and_kind.length_vacuity: The packet claims no 10.2.1.3 truncation or blank-padding effect. Where character assignment appears as an eligibility or control plan, S10.2.1.2-006 and S10.2.1.2-007 require explicit LEN checks and warn against relying on blank-padded character comparison, which would be vacuous.
character_length_and_kind.kind_availability: No plan assumes ISO 10646 or ASCII kinds exist. S10.2.1.2-007 is profile-qualified and uses only supported character kinds, skipping unavailable-kind facets rather than approximating them.
character_length_and_kind.verdict: no vacuous character-length oracle and no unsupported-kind assumption found

oracle_discipline.side_effects_calls_and_order: No plan relies on side effects, call counts, temporaries, simultaneity or evaluation order. The elemental defined-assignment plans in 10.2.1.5 inspect only final corresponding element values and explicitly forbid order and call-count oracles.
oracle_discipline.allocatable_reallocation: Allocatable same-rank and deferred-length cases are treated as eligibility and admission rules only. The required deallocation, allocation, resulting shape, bounds, type and length effects remain with 10.2.1.3, while the coarray and coindexed unallocated-allocatable prohibitions are correctly recorded as 10.2.1.2 restrictions. No effect claim belonging to 10.2.1.3 appears here.

nonblocking_observations.observation: Future fixtures must preserve the exact Table 10.8 enum-row wording: when expr is integer, a primary in expr shall be an enumerator of the enum type. Do not narrow it to arbitrary integers, and do not narrow it accidentally to only a bare enumerator primary.
